identity.title: Bitangents of real algebraic curves: signed count and constructions

findings.title: Rational limiting chords need not specialize to rational bitangents
findings.source_claim: For any field K of characteristic not2, a specified limiting chord defined over K deforms to a K-bitangent of Ct for t in K.
hypotheses: Exact Newton triangle, smooth compactified two-section, eight distinct simple rational ramification values; no additional chord-concurrency condition is stated.
Ct:(y^2-xz)^2-t^2*product(x-a^2*z)=0 is exactly the Proposition3.6 family.
All Ct with0<t<3/25 are smooth over C; generic dual certified originally at t=1/1000 and hence outside finitely many parameters.
Specified rational chords y=(2/5)(x+z) and y=(3/10)(x+z).
The exact quadratic-square equivalence is used only for 0<|t|<3/25, where the V^4 coefficient is nonzero.
findings.decisive_evidence: Unique nearby branches y=m_plus/minus(t)(x+z) have m_plus/minus(t)^2=1/8 +/- (7/200)*sqrt(1-625*t^2/9). For t=1/N,N>=105,(3N-1)^2<9N^2-625<(3N)^2, so both normalized coefficients are irrational. The exact square restriction gives two distinct real contacts. A nearby line y=h*U+ell*V with ell!=0 necessarily satisfies (625/9)*(h^2-1)^2=16*(1+ell^2)^2, which is excluded in fixed neighborhoods of both limiting chords. No alternative rational nearby branch exists. The square-equivalence domain is 0<|t|<3/25; all t=1/N,N>=105 lie in it.
findings.proof: ReportSection3 proves all admissibility, square condition, irrationality, uniqueness, smoothness from nonzero Ciani principal minors, ordinary contacts, and mod13 projective Hessian transversality at t=1/1000. Both retained exact independent calculation programs exited0. The nongeneric parameter set is finite, so generic irrational specializations occur arbitrarily close to0. The report's former t!=0 intermediate equivalence has been corrected to 0<|t|<3/25; the excluded t=3/25 example is (UV/5)^2 with q=1/36.
findings.impact: Invalidates the asserted arithmetic extension and proposed per-chord K-bitangent bound. Does not refute the real signed-count and deformation theorems; does not claim the whole quartic has no other Q-bitangents.

repair.verified: In this example both branches belong to Q[[t]]. Formal or appropriate Henselian lifting requires its own hypotheses and does not imply Q-rational specialization.
repair.boundary: Restriction to formal/Henselian or suitable analytic settings materially narrows the arithmetic claim. No assertion about the unacquired journal version or author adoption.

findings.title: The prescribed number of non-real roots can be odd
findings.source_claim: Real degree-k small perturbations R1,R2 with simple roots and floor(k/2) non-real roots.
hypotheses: R1,R2 real polynomials with only simple roots
findings.decisive_evidence: Each polynomial would need exactly one non-real root, impossible because non-real roots of a real polynomial come in conjugate pairs. Same obstruction for k congruent2or3 mod4.
findings.proof: ReportSection4 gives exact real polynomials with floor(k/2) conjugate pairs and independently proves the required real critical-point counts: odd quotient theta H(theta^2) strictly increasing and unramified at infinity, even quotient H(theta^2) has exactly0 and infinity as simple critical points. H(z)=product((z+a_j)/(1+b_j z)),a_j,b_j>0,a_jb_j<1.
findings.impact: Impossible local prescription in the proof. Corrected real polynomials exist with original degrees and arbitrary closeness; no counterexample to Lemma4.7 or Proposition1.6.

repair.verified: Use floor(k/2) pairs, with explicit monotone factors. For odd k a small real Mobius domain change moves the pole at infinity and gives both affine degrees exactlyk.
repair.boundary: Full node placement and Brusotti smoothing remain external geometric dependencies. The source diagrams have now been inspected. No claim that every polynomial with corrected root count automatically has the required critical points.

problems.independent_check: Root independently follows the degree-eight hyperelliptic degeneration, its eight simple distinct rational critical values and the exact nearby quartic restriction.
